candidates.api_shape: miura_cell(a, b, gamma_deg, fold_deg) -> four parallelogram plates + hinges, 1 DoF
candidates.fdm: Four plates, living_hinge or LET at the creases. Prints flat. Pose is fold angle. Tile n x m for a sheet; the tile is the primitive, the wing is a product.
candidates.name: miura_cell
candidates.why: Miura-ori, 1970 / map fold. Rigid-foldable degree-4 vertex, one DoF, packs a sheet into a stack. Solar arrays, folding maps, sandwich cores. auxetic_panel is a hole lattice, not a crease pose. The missing origami cell.

candidates.api_shape: kresling_cell(n_sides, height, twist_deg) -> a triangulated cylinder, often bistable
candidates.fdm: A tube of triangles, living hinges on the creases. Prints as a net or standing. Twist-compress is the pose. Bistable if the geometry says so.
candidates.name: kresling_cell
candidates.why: Kresling twist-buckle. Non-rigid origami, the named origami actuator / bellows. Distinct from sarrus (bar fold, exact line) and from bistable_beam (planar snap). Deployable booms, crawling robots, pumps.

candidates.api_shape: yoshimura_cell(n, diamond) -> a diamond-tube that flattens
candidates.fdm: Prints as a net of diamonds. Structural boom, crash tube. Less of an actuator than Kresling.
candidates.name: yoshimura_cell
candidates.why: Yoshimura diamond pattern. The other named origami tube. Packs flat, carries load. After Miura and Kresling, the third tessellation people search.

candidates.api_shape: waterbomb_vertex(r, fold_deg) -> a 6-crease vertex that bumps out of plane
candidates.fdm: Six sectors, living hinges. Prints flat. Used as a gripper bump or a tessellated surface.
candidates.name: waterbomb_vertex
candidates.why: Waterbomb / balloon vertex. Not rigid-foldable the same way as Miura. Soft-robot and texture cell.

candidates.api_shape: stem_boom(r, slit, coil_r) -> a slit tube that coils on a drum and locks when straight
candidates.fdm: PETG/TPU thin wall, or a bought steel tape. Pose is pay-out. tape_spring is the hinge; STEM is the boom.
candidates.name: stem_boom
candidates.why: Storable tubular extendible member. Coilable boom, the deployable cousin of Negator (which wants to coil) and tape-spring (which wants to stay straight). Antenna / camera masts.

candidates.api_shape: a radial sector of a flasher; a full flasher is a product
candidates.fdm: Prints as a net. Compact wrap of a disc.
candidates.name: flasher_sector
candidates.why: Flasher origami. One sector is a cell; wrapping a whole solar disc is a product. After Miura.

candidates.api_shape: a ring of 6+ tetrahedra, Bricard inversion
candidates.fdm: Prints as tetrahedra with hinges. Toy / teaching.
candidates.name: kaleidocycle
candidates.why: Named Bricard ring. After bricard_6r, a style, not a second topology.

candidates.name: hoberman_sphere
candidates.why: Spatial slice already rejected this. The cell is angulated_scissor. lazy_tongs is the straight special case.

candidates.name: lazy_tongs_again
candidates.why: Straight scissor. Not a crease pattern.

candidates.name: auxetic_as_miura
candidates.why: Reentrant metamaterial, not a rigid-origami pose. Keep both.

rejected.name: satellite_solar_wing
rejected.why: A tiled Miura plus a spacecraft. Product. miura_cell is the primitive.

summary:
A deployable is a 1-DoF (or few-DoF) mechanism that packs small and opens large. Two families: bar-and-scissor (Hoberman, lazy-tongs, Bennett/Bricard rings) and origami tessellations (rigid-foldable sheets: Miura, flasher, Yoshimura; non-rigid: Kresling, waterbomb). Pellegrino/You treat the reusable object as a unit cell; the sphere, canopy, or satellite is a product. Spatial slice already named angulated_scissor (Hoberman kinked cell) and Bennett/Bricard rings. Flexure slice named LET and tape-spring. This slice owns the crease-pattern cells that are not those.

Catalog already has the bar special cases and two sheet tricks. lazy_tongs is the straight-scissor (kink=180). sarrus is a spatial fold that makes a line, not a pack. iris_diaphragm is an aperture of blades, not a crease pattern. auxetic_panel is a metamaterial lattice (reentrant), related in spirit to Miura but not a rigid-origami pose. kerf_bend_cutter is a living-hinge slit lattice. Grep finds no Miura, Kresling, Yoshimura, flasher, waterbomb, STEM boom, or kaleidocycle.

FDM reality. Miura-ori unit (four parallelograms, one mountain and three valleys at a degree-4 vertex) is rigid-foldable, 1 DoF, prints as four plates plus living hinges or LET joints; pose is the fold angle. That is the solar-array / map-fold cell. Kresling is a twist-buckled cylinder, non-rigid, often bistable, prints as a tube of triangles; the named origami actuator. Yoshimura is a diamond-tube that flattens; structural boom cell. Flasher wraps a disc into a compact spiral; one cell is a radial sector, a full flasher is getting product-shaped. Waterbomb is a 6-crease vertex, used as a bump / gripper cell. STEM / CTM coilable boom is a tape-spring cousin (slit tube that coils on a drum). Kaleidocycle is a Bricard ring of tetrahedra; after bricard_6r, a named toy cell. A Hoberman sphere or a Miura solar wing is a product. Inflatable deployables are out.
title: Deployables, origami, and foldable cells
